title: Density control method for compression test of compacted lime-flyash stabilised fiber-soil mixtures
author: Kafodya, Okonta

steps.title: Characterize soil properties
steps.instruction: Characterize the soil according to ASTM D1140‑17 to confirm suitability for lime stabilization.

steps.title: Determine Proctor optimum moisture
steps.instruction: Perform a standard Proctor test (ASTM D698) to obtain the maximum dry density (MDD) and optimum moisture content (OMC); record MDD ≈1870 kg/m³ and OMC ≈12 %.

steps.title: Find minimum lime demand
steps.instruction: Conduct the Eades‑Grim test (ASTM D6276) to estimate the minimum lime requirement for the soil.

steps.title: Prepare stabilizer mix
steps.instruction: Mix hydrated lime Ca(OH)₂ and class F fly ash in a mass ratio of 1 : 2; add sisal fibers at 0.75 % of the total stabilized‑soil mass (use ρ = mf/ms) and blend manually with the soil at the OMC until a homogeneous composite is obtained.

steps.title: Mellow mixture
steps.instruction: Place the composite in a waterproof airtight plastic bag and let it rest for 1 hour to reach flocculation equilibrium.

steps.title: Calibrate compaction load
steps.instruction: Prepare trial specimens at the OMC and compact each layer using a load‑gauge at pressures of 1.5, 3, 5, 7.5, 10 MPa; measure bulk density (ρb) and compute dry density with ρ = 100 ρb/(100 + w) where w = OMC; fit the regression σ = 12.5×10³ P/D (P in tons, D in mm²) and the dry‑density‑pressure relationship (R² = 99 % for 1700–2040 kg/m³).

steps.title: Estimate required pressure
steps.instruction: Using the regression model, estimate the compaction pressure needed to achieve the target MDD of 1870 kg/m³; the model predicts ≈4 MPa.

steps.title: Prepare UCS specimens
steps.instruction: Fill 1 : 2.5 diameter‑to‑height molds with the composite at 12 % OMC; compact each layer to 4 MPa using the load gauge; fabricate at least three specimens (minimum two per ASTM 5102, three optimal).

steps.title: Record and evaluate densities
steps.instruction: Measure the dry density of each specimen; for 70 specimens the mean density was 1854.88 kg/m³ (CV = 0.029, SD = 54.4 kg/m³) with 30 ≥ target and 40 < target; acceptable range is 1815.5–1924.5 kg/m³ (±3 % of 1870 kg/m³).

steps.title: Assess probability of success
steps.instruction: Apply the binomial model P(x,n,p)= n! pˣ(1‑p)^{n‑x}/[x!(n‑x)!] with p = 0.62 (failure probability 0.38) for 70 specimens; for three specimens the probability of obtaining at least two densities within ±3 % is acceptable. CV variations of 2.9 %, 1.9 % and 0.9 % correspond to success probabilities 0.62, 0.37 and 0.13 respectively.

steps.title: Avoid manual rammer errors
steps.instruction: Do not use manual rammers (4.5 kg/2.5 kg) for compaction counting; instead use the load‑gauge method to apply a constant pressure and eliminate counting errors.
